issues.description: Method addAnimal(Animal): The UML in problem_statement.md declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the reference implementation in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines public void addAnimal(Animal animal). This inconsistency between the UML in the problem statement (boolean) and the implemented signature (void) will confuse students about the expected return type and whether they should return a boolean value when implementing the method. The template Farm.java contains a TODO placeholder for implementing the Farm class and does not provide a conflicting implementation, but the authoritative solution and tests (if any) expect the void signature as implemented in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred resolution: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void to match the solution and the textual examples that call addAnimal without using a return value. Alternatively (if a boolean return is intended pedagogically), update the template and solution to implement public boolean addAnimal(Animal) and adjust any call sites, examples, and tests accordingly. Document the chosen contract in the problem text so students know whether to return a boolean.
